brief: Part: mounting plate. Material: aluminium 6061-T6. Dimensions: L = 70 mm, W = 50 mm, T = 4 mm. Features: 4x diameter 4 mm through holes on a 56 x 36 mm pattern, centred. Load: none.

intent.summary: A flat aluminium plate intended to mount or space a component using four through-holes in a bolt pattern, with no specified applied load.
stated: Hole pattern: 56 x 36 mm, centred on plate
implied: 4 through holes on a bolt pattern implies it is fastened with bolts/screws to another flat surface, so it needs reasonably flat, coplanar mounting faces
Plate dimensions (70x50) vs hole pattern (56x36) imply symmetric edge margins (7 mm and 7 mm on length sides, 7 mm on width sides), suggesting a centred, symmetric layout
Specifying a precise material grade (6061-T6) implies some structural or environmental requirement exists even though load is stated as none
unstated: What the plate mounts to and what it mounts (the mating component/assembly)
Fastener type and size intended for the 4 mm holes (clearance vs tapped, bolt grade)
Whether 'load: none' means truly static/decorative use or simply that loads were not characterized
Flatness/parallelism tolerance on the mounting faces
General dimensional tolerances for length, width, thickness, and hole positions
Hole edge treatment (chamfer, deburr) and through-hole tolerance class (clearance fit for what fastener)
Whether the plate requires electrical grounding/continuity or insulation
Orientation of the plate in use (horizontal, vertical, overhead)
Any need for countersinking or counterboring for flush fastener heads
Quantity/production method (machined, waterjet, etc.) which affects achievable tolerances
risk_signals: 'Load: none' is stated but not substantiated — if the plate is later used to carry or support a load despite this label, the design would be unverified for that case
No information on orientation (e.g., overhead mounting) is given, so a safety-relevant use (e.g., mounting over a person or carrying suspended equipment) cannot be ruled out from the brief alone

requirements.statement: The plate shall be 70 mm long in X.
requirements.rationale: Brief states L = 70 mm as the overall plate length.

requirements.statement: The plate shall be 50 mm wide in Y.
requirements.rationale: Brief states W = 50 mm as the overall plate width.

requirements.statement: The plate shall be 4 mm thick overall.
requirements.rationale: Brief states T = 4 mm; for a flat plate this is the whole part's Z extent.

requirements.statement: The four mounting holes shall each be 4 mm in diameter.
requirements.rationale: Brief states 4x diameter 4 mm through holes.

requirements.statement: The mounting hole pattern shall span 56 mm in X, centred on the plate.
requirements.rationale: Brief states a 56 x 36 mm hole pattern, centred.

requirements.statement: The mounting hole pattern shall span 36 mm in Y, centred on the plate.
requirements.rationale: Brief states a 56 x 36 mm hole pattern, centred.

requirements.statement: The plate shall have exactly four mounting through-holes.
requirements.rationale: Brief specifies 4x through holes on the bolt pattern.

assumptions.statement: The plate carries no structural load; it is used purely for mounting/spacing with static, low-energy service.
assumptions.rationale: The brief explicitly states 'Load: none', answering the question rather than leaving it silent.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If a real load is later applied, the plate thickness and hole edge distances have not been checked against any margin and may be inadequate.

assumptions.statement: The 4 mm through holes are plain clearance holes (not tapped) sized for an M4 fastener, with no counterbore or countersink.
assumptions.rationale: A 4 mm through hole on a bolt-pattern mounting plate is conventionally a clearance hole for an M4 screw unless stated otherwise.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If the holes were meant to be tapped or sized for a different fastener, hole tolerance and thread callouts would need rework.

assumptions.statement: The plate is left as-machined with no specified coating, anodizing, or special surface finish.
assumptions.rationale: No finish is called out in the brief; as-machined aluminium is the conventional default absent a stated requirement.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If corrosion protection or cosmetic finish is actually required, the part would need re-processing.

assumptions.statement: General (non-called-out) dimensions and hole positions follow standard machine-shop tolerancing (approx. ±0.1 mm linear).
assumptions.rationale: The brief gives nominal dimensions only, with no tolerance block; standard shop tolerance is the conventional default for a simple plate.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: Tighter tolerances, if actually required (e.g. for a precision fixture), would require re-specifying and re-manufacturing.

assumptions.statement: No special flatness/parallelism callout or mounting orientation constraint applies beyond ordinary machining practice; the plate may be mounted in any orientation.
assumptions.rationale: The brief gives no flatness tolerance or orientation requirement, and the stated absence of load removes any structural reason to constrain orientation.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If the plate must be mounted overhead or bear a flatness-critical interface, additional callouts would be needed.

document.name: Mounting plate
document.description: Flat aluminium mounting plate, 70 x 50 x 4 mm, with a 56 x 36 mm bolt pattern of four 4 mm clearance holes centred on the plate.

parameters.description: Diameter of each of the four mounting through-holes
Bolt pattern span in X, centred on the plate
Bolt pattern span in Y, centred on the plate

interfaces.description: Four-hole 56 x 36 mm bolt pattern, centred on the plate, for clearance fasteners sized to mounting_hole_diameter.

answer.rationale: The plate is a single box primitive sized by plate_length/plate_width/plate_thickness (thickness last, as required for a flat plate), and the four mounting holes are a chain of four separate `hole` features (each tagged "mounting" and consuming the previous one) rather than a pattern, since the hole-count requirement counts tagged features individually. Each hole's position is driven directly from hole_pattern_x/2 and hole_pattern_y/2 so the pattern stays centred and parametric if those or the plate size change; holes are cut last, after the solid base, per the cut-holes-last rule. The declared REQ_ROUND requirement does not match this rectangular plate geometry from the brief, so it was left to fail honestly rather than deforming the part's shape to game it.

note: A correct 70 x 50 x 4 plate held to be round: 'T = 4 mm' and 'diameter 4 mm through holes' -- the holes' 4 was read as the part's size, and it matched the plate's thickness.
